TH Khan with Afzal Hossain Khan, Advocates-----For the Petitioner.
Mrinal Kanti Biswas, Advocate-----For Opposite—Parties.
parties:
Md. Khorshed Ali ----- Petitioners
Vs
Administrator of Waqf ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment: 6. Mr TH Khan with Mr Afzal Hossain khan, the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the petitioner submitted that the Courts below committing gross error both in law and facts occasioning failure of justice. In course of argument the learned Counsels placed the judgments of the Courts below with a short background of the case that after the death of Meer Nawab Ali, his son Khizir Ali for himself and for and on behalf of his two daughters Syeda Sharfunnessa and Syeda Fatema Faizunnessa became co-plaintiffs in the Title Suit No. 9 of 1963 filed by the then Mutawalli against the Government in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka which being transferred to the 5th Court of Sub-ordinate Judge was renumbered as Title Suit No. 34 of 1964, in respect of their properties and ultimately the said suit had been decreed on contest wherein 3 annas share in the suit properties were declared in favour of them; the defendant No. 3 is the husband of the aforesaid Sharfunnessa and on the basis of that relationship the defendant is doing all mischief as stated elaborately in the plaint by misusing his official designation; and undue influence, has been trying to take illegal advantage and in pursuance thereof got the aforesaid two letters written to your petitioner directing him to demarcate the lands of Meer Nawab Ali form the Waqf property and hand over possession to them and he also applied to the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka requesting him the same thing and the Deputy Commissioner, by his "জেঃ প্রঃ ঢা: / রাঃ ৬/ ২৬৬ / ২০০৪-২০০৬ তারিখ ২৮-৭-২০০৪” directed him to get the matter decided in a Civil Court (which means that they are to file a partition Suit for the purpose); The learned Counsel also contended that the plaintiffs claim in the suit having been outside the scope of sections 32, 34 and 35 of the Waqf Ordinance the Courts below erred in law resulting in the error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in dismissing the suit as barred by limitation for non-filing of any appeal under section 32(10) of the Waqf Ordinance. The learned Counsel also contended that about 50% of the Waqf properties having been outside the control of the Mutawalli for which litigations are continuing in the Courts of law, and 3 annas of the disputed properties having been the private properties amalgated with properties in Waqf, the Courts below erred in law in not rejecting the application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure filed by the defendant No. 3 before filing written statement in the suit, and in not directing the defendants to file a Partition Suit in the Civil Court for the purpose. The learned Counsel lastly argued that in the facts and circumstances of the case the Courts below erred in law resulting in the error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in not rejecting the application under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, holding that the plaintiff's claim in respect of the two letters challenged in the suit are outside the scope of previsions relating to the appeal, and, as such, the application is not maintainable; as the Administrator has got no authority to remove the Mutawalli for non-compliance of his order relating to properties outside the waqf. In support of his contention the referred 13 BLT 507 and 11 MLR (AD) 206.
